summary: Created one evidence-linked AI infrastructure and power-bottleneck idea. Current IEA and issuer evidence confirms concentrated load growth and strong supplier orders, margins, and cash conversion, but valuation, customer concentration, capacity additions, and backlog conversion keep the investment conclusion security-specific. Enqueued bounded GE Vernova, Eaton, and post-Q2 Vertiv research; no relationship, strategy, signal, or paper order was created.

evidence.source: International Energy Agency, Key Questions on Energy and AI
evidence.claim: The IEA's April 2026 central case projects data-centre electricity use rising from about 485 TWh in 2025 to 950 TWh in 2030, with AI-focused facilities tripling consumption, while near-term bottlenecks constrain more aggressive scenarios.

evidence.source: International Energy Agency, Energy and AI
evidence.claim: The IEA estimates around 20% of planned data-centre projects could face delays unless grid risks are addressed and emphasizes the concentrated local impact of data-centre load.

GE Vernova reported USD 24.2 billion of orders, a USD 13.0 billion sequential backlog increase, USD 176 billion total backlog, USD 5.1 billion free cash flow, and more than USD 5 billion of year-to-date data-centre orders.
Eaton reported backlog growth of 44% in Electrical Americas and 73% in Electrical Global, with Electrical Americas data-centre orders up about 240%.

Vertiv reported 30% sales growth, a 430-basis-point increase in adjusted operating margin to 20.8%, and USD 653 million of adjusted free cash flow; its next quarterly release was scheduled after this review.

daily_report_items: Researched AI infrastructure and power bottlenecks: physical demand and supplier order conversion are confirmed, but valuation and backlog-quality gates block a strategy; queued GE Vernova, Eaton, and Vertiv research.
